chunks: And from him, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, and Ali ibn Khalid al-Aqouli, from Karram, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similar to it.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the pregnant woman whose husband dies, is there for her expenses (nafaqah)? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.
ai.seo_question: Does a pregnant widow receive financial maintenance during her waiting period?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that a pregnant widow is not entitled to financial maintenance (nafaqah) during her waiting period (iddah), distinguishing this ruling from that of a divorced woman. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan school of hadith, linking Imam al-Sadiq through prominent narrators like Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it underscores that the husband's obligation to provide for his wife is tied to the continuity of the marital bond, which ends upon death.
